table.title: [Estimated Population of China at Various Dates, 1381-1928]
table.caption_extra: Population. "The subjoined tables show the estimated population at various dates and the latest official estimates of the population :—"
transcriber_notes: Rows: 26 as printed.
No total printed.

Layout: re-checked against tight crops of leaf p0024. The table is printed as a single list in the left-hand column of the page (year, a row of leader dots, population), not as side-by-side blocks; there are no ditto marks, braces, footnote marks or repeated years, and each year carries exactly one figure. It is therefore kept as one two-column grid; leader dots omitted.
No column headings are printed; 'Year' and 'Population' are supplied by the transcriber. 'A.D.' is printed after the first year only (1381 A.D.) and is kept there as printed.

Printed sequence kept as is, including the abrupt jumps (e.g. 28,241,000 for 1711 then 125,046,000 for 1736; 103,050,000 for 1753 between 157,343,000 for 1743 and 143,125,000 for 1760); these are as printed, not transcription errors.
table.context: This list opens the "Population" section of Chapter I, General Information (printed p. 1), under the heading "POPULATION" and directly after the "Area" paragraph. The book introduces it by noting that "the taking of a census by the methods adopted in Western nations has never yet been attempted in China, and consequently estimates of the total population have varied to an extraordinary degree"; the list is offered simply as "the estimated population at various dates", with no source named for any individual figure. That caveat is the book's only explanation for the uneven series, which swings from about 21 to 28 million in 1662-1711 to 125 million in 1736 and falls and rises again several times before reaching 485,508,000 for 1928. The list is followed on the same page by the "Area and Population of China" table by province, which the book says is "compiled from figures issued by the Ministry of Interior in 1936".
